main.title: Red Steel 2
main.subtitle: A sword and a revolver share the view
main.summary: Red Steel 2 is Ubisoft Paris' Wii first-person action game combining sword fighting and gunplay in a stylised setting that mixes western towns with samurai traditions. The player follows the last surviving Kusagari warrior through Caldera, confronting enemies with both a firearm and a blade. MotionPlus is required, allowing the direction and force of a swing to matter during close combat. The new setting stands apart from the first Red Steel's story, building its identity around a fighter who can move between shooting and a physical exchange of sword strikes.

cards.heading: A sword and a revolver share the view
cards.text: Red Steel 2 is Ubisoft Paris' Wii first-person action game combining sword fighting and gunplay in a stylised setting that mixes western towns with samurai traditions. The player follows the last surviving Kusagari warrior through Caldera, confronting enemies with both a firearm and a blade. MotionPlus is required, allowing the direction and force of a swing to matter during close combat. The new setting stands apart from the first Red Steel's story, building its identity around a fighter who can move between shooting and a physical exchange of sword strikes.

cards.heading: A guarded enemy asks for another angle
cards.text: Different opponents resist attacks in different ways. A defensive blade position can require a particular direction of slash, while heavy armour must be broken with forceful swings. Successful sequences can stun a foe and create an opening for a finishing gesture. The player therefore has to read the enemy before committing to another attack. Gunfire and sword techniques occupy the same encounter, giving distance and vulnerability practical importance. A confident response comes from recognising which action will open the opponent rather than repeating the same movement regardless of its effect.

cards.heading: Practise the technique before taking it outside
cards.text: Safe houses offer new moves, weapons and armour, along with wanted posters that lead to optional work. Purchasing a technique sends the player to a training area to practise its required sequence, connecting an upgrade with the movement needed to use it. Money earned through combat and exploration finances further improvements, while replayable challenges provide another opportunity to develop those skills. The structure breaks the action into expeditions and preparation, giving the increasingly capable warrior a place to rehearse before returning to the next group of opponents in Caldera.

main.title: Just Cause 2
main.summary: Just Cause 2 is a 2010 action-adventure video game developed by Avalanche Studios and published by Square Enix.

cards.heading: Rico returns as Avalanche rebuilds Just Cause
cards.text: Just Cause 2 is Avalanche Studios' 2010 open-world action game, published by Square Enix. Rico Rodriguez arrives in the island nation of Panau to challenge dictator Baby Panay and confront his former mentor Tom Sheldon. Guns, a grappling hook and a parachute let the player connect objects, launch into the air and improvise attacks across the landscape. Missions and the destruction of government property build Chaos points. The sequel reworked the first game's systems around a larger Southeast Asian-inspired setting, making movement and disruption central to its approach.

cards.heading: Chaos links destruction to campaign progression
cards.text: Just Cause 2 is a third-person action-adventure game in which players control Rico Rodriguez, field operative of the Agency, in an effort to overthrow the island dictatorship of Panau: an open world for players to explore. The game has three types of missions. Agency missions advance the story and are the game's main campaign; faction missions task players to assist the game's three factions, and stronghold missions task players to infiltrate government bases and liberate them for the factions. To advance through the campaign missions a player must earn chaos points, a progression system introduced in the game. Players earn chaos points for completing missions and destroying designated government property. As the number of chaos points increases, the factions gain influence and the government begins to collapse. In addition to typical missions, Just Cause 2 has race challenges which give players cash.

cards.heading: A grappling hook and parachute work together
cards.text: Just Cause 2 includes a grappling hook enabling players to tether objects together. In a high-speed vehicle chase a player can use the grappling hook to attach the pursuit vehicle to the ground, forcing it to stop and often damaging it by flipping. Players can also tether two enemies together. The grappling hook allows a player to pull himself, hold onto objects such as walls or helicopters and pull enemies towards Rico. The player has a parachute, which can be instantly deployed and repacked. This can be combined with the grappling hook as quick transport, with players "slingshotting" themselves into the air.

main.title: Etrian Odyssey III: The Drowned City
main.subtitle: A guild faces the drowned city
main.summary: Etrian Odyssey III: The Drowned City is Atlus's Nintendo DS dungeon role-playing game about a player-created guild investigating the labyrinth beneath Armoroad. The first-person journey and hand-drawn touchscreen map return, now joined by seafaring exploration and a new set of character classes. A party of up to five adventurers represents a larger guild whose members can be changed in town. The structure keeps preparation close to discovery: the next expedition begins with a choice of people and supplies as well as a destination on the map.

cards.heading: A guild faces the drowned city
cards.text: Etrian Odyssey III: The Drowned City is Atlus's Nintendo DS dungeon role-playing game about a player-created guild investigating the labyrinth beneath Armoroad. The first-person journey and hand-drawn touchscreen map return, now joined by seafaring exploration and a new set of character classes. A party of up to five adventurers represents a larger guild whose members can be changed in town. The structure keeps preparation close to discovery: the next expedition begins with a choice of people and supplies as well as a destination on the map.

cards.heading: Choose the people behind the map
cards.text: The new classes provide different skills, equipment and statistics, while subclassing later allows most characters to combine part of another role with their own. Those choices affect what the party can accomplish during encounters and how safely it can sustain an expedition. A guild can retain more members than it takes into the labyrinth, allowing another group to be prepared for a different purpose. The hand-drawn record of the route is shared, but the group following it can change as the player understands what lies farther below.

cards.heading: Navigation becomes a second adventure
cards.text: The mapping tools include symbols for currents, landmarks and notes, supporting the game's interest in routes as well as rooms. Recording what has been found makes a future journey more predictable, while another unexamined direction keeps the larger area uncertain. The combination gives the series' patient exploration another setting beyond its familiar corridors. Etrian Odyssey III treats both the guild and its map as things built through play. Each expedition can return with a stronger character, a better plan and a small piece of information that makes the next departure possible.

main.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Conviction
main.subtitle: When Sam Fisher Stops Waiting in the Shadows
main.summary: Ubisoft gives Sam Fisher a more aggressive stealth game, using Mark and Execute and Last Known Position to turn observation into rapid attacks.

cards.heading: Sam becomes a fugitive
cards.text: Splinter Cell: Conviction reached Xbox 360 in North America on April 13, 2010. Sam Fisher operates as a fugitive, observing enemies before striking quickly and escaping. Mark and Execute, Last Known Position and objectives projected onto surfaces give the player information for planning those attacks. The faster approach divided fans of the earlier games' slower infiltration.

cards.heading: Preparing an attack from shadow
cards.text: Darkness helps Sam prepare an attack and move away afterwards. The player studies nearby guards, chooses when to strike and tries to break contact before they can respond. This pace places more emphasis on taking the initiative while retaining stealth and surveillance as tools.

cards.heading: Mark and Execute
cards.text: A close-quarters takedown earns a use of Mark and Execute. The player can then mark targets and eliminate them in a rapid sequence. Choosing targets and a starting position becomes the important preparation for that automated burst of fire.

cards.heading: The last place they saw Sam
cards.text: After Sam is spotted and escapes, a silhouette marks the last place enemies saw him. Guards investigate that position while the player moves elsewhere. The display shows what the enemy believes, making detection a situation that can be used for misdirection rather than an automatic end to an attempt.

main.title: NieR
main.subtitle: Two versions of one ruined world
main.summary: Nier is a 2010 action role-playing game developed by Cavia and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360.

cards.heading: Two versions of one ruined world
cards.text:
Nier is a 2010 action role-playing game developed by Cavia and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. In Japan, the game was released as Nier Replicant for the PlayStation 3 with a younger main character, while an alternative version titled Nier Gestalt with an older main character was released for the Xbox 360; Gestalt was released outside Japan as Nier for both platforms. A remaster of the Replicant version called Nier Replicant ver.1.22474487139... was released internationally for PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Windows in 2021.

The game is a spin-off from the Drakengard series, following the fifth ending of the first game, the events of which have left Earth in ruin. Set over a thousand years later, the story follows the player-named protagonist attempting to find a cure for a terminal illness afflicting a young girl named Yonah. The gameplay borrows elements from various video game genres, occasionally switching between them and the main role-playing-based gameplay.

cards.heading: A changing viewpoint
cards.text: Nier is an action role-playing game in which players take on the role of a player-named protagonist; the protagonist is a middle-aged man in Nier Gestalt and a teenage boy in Nier Replicant, named by the player. The player directly controls the main character through a third-person perspective to interact with people, objects, and enemies throughout the game. The player can turn the camera around the characters, which allows for a 360° view of the surroundings. The three-dimensional world is divided into areas separated by loading screens, and the player can move freely throughout these areas by walking, running, jumping, and climbing ladders. In some rooms and buildings, the camera swings to the side, and the main character is restricted to moving as in a two-dimensional platforming environment, while during certain battles, the camera pulls up to simulate a top-down shoot 'em up or other video game genres.

cards.heading: Yoko Taro, Cavia and MONACA
cards.text: Beginning production in 2007, the game was directed by Drakengard creator Yoko Taro, who was given a lot of creative freedom with the project. Its storyline drew inspiration from the September 11 attacks and the war on terror, while its gameplay was partly inspired by the God of War series. Due to feedback outside of Japan, multiple versions of the protagonist were created. The music was composed by Monaca, a music studio founded by Keiichi Okabe, with several albums being released.

main.title: Super Street Fighter IV
main.subtitle: Expanding the Street Fighter IV roster
main.summary: Super Street Fighter IV reached PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in North America on April 27, 2010.

cards.heading: A revised Street Fighter IV
cards.text: Super Street Fighter IV reached PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in North America on April 27, 2010. Capcom expanded the previous game with ten fighters, a second Ultra Combo choice for each character, revised online modes and balance changes. Its lower price reflected a substantial revision aimed in part at players who already owned Street Fighter IV.

cards.heading: Ten additional fighters
cards.text: Juri and Hakan join returning characters including Dudley, Ibuki, Makoto, Cody and Guy. Their different ranges, speeds and tools introduce new matchups for the existing roster. Players can keep familiar characters while learning how the expanded cast changes the competition.

cards.heading: Choosing an Ultra Combo
cards.text: Before a match, each fighter chooses between two Ultra Combos. Their different ranges and uses change the threat once the meter becomes available. Players must consider both their own choice and the option selected by an opponent.

cards.heading: Rebalancing the competition
cards.text: Capcom adjusted damage, priorities and other properties after a year of tournaments and online play. These changes aimed to address weaknesses and excesses while preserving familiar characters. The revised balance gave competitors new situations to test within the established fighting system.

main.title: Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker 2
main.subtitle: A competition begins with a crash
main.summary: Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker 2 is Tose's Nintendo DS role-playing game following another aspiring monster scout toward a major competition. An airship journey instead ends on an unfamiliar island, leaving the protagonist to search for survivors and explore its inhabitants. Recruiting Dragon Quest creatures again provides the team that fights on his behalf. The interrupted journey gives the collection another immediate purpose: a capable group of monsters is needed to move through the island, understand what has happened and prepare for the challenges awaiting beyond the first safe area.

cards.heading: A competition begins with a crash
cards.text: Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker 2 is Tose's Nintendo DS role-playing game following another aspiring monster scout toward a major competition. An airship journey instead ends on an unfamiliar island, leaving the protagonist to search for survivors and explore its inhabitants. Recruiting Dragon Quest creatures again provides the team that fights on his behalf. The interrupted journey gives the collection another immediate purpose: a capable group of monsters is needed to move through the island, understand what has happened and prepare for the challenges awaiting beyond the first safe area.

cards.heading: A large monster occupies more than one place
cards.text: The team still has three spaces, but new large and gargantuan creatures can occupy two or all three of them. Choosing one changes the shape of the entire group, trading a larger individual presence against the flexibility of several smaller companions. Players can issue direct battle commands or choose tactics for the monsters to follow. The human scout supports them with items. Size therefore becomes a practical part of preparing the party, giving another reason to think about how its members work together before the next turn-based encounter begins.

cards.heading: Another version extends the same expedition
cards.text: The Japanese Professional edition added further monsters, regions and abilities while retaining the main story, extending the same island adventure rather than replacing its premise. The original game also supported direct multiplayer battles, giving a developed team another kind of opponent. Exploring, recruiting and preparing remain closely connected: an unfamiliar creature can become a useful addition, while a new arrangement may make another part of the island easier to approach. The sequel develops that cycle through the changed party sizes and the opportunities offered by its interrupted journey.

main.title: Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker
main.summary: Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker is a 2010 action-adventure stealth game developed by Kojima Productions and published by Konami for the PlayStation Portable.

cards.heading: Snake builds Militaires Sans Fronti?res
cards.text: Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker is a 2010 action-adventure stealth game developed by Kojima Productions and published by Konami for the PlayStation Portable. Written, directed, and designed by Hideo Kojima, it is the seventh mainline Metal Gear game and serves as a narrative sequel to Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater (2004) and Metal Gear Solid: Portable Ops (2006). Set in 1974, the game follows returning protagonist Snake as he operates the private mercenary organization Militaires Sans Frontières (MSF). When a heavily armed paramilitary force occupies Costa Rica, Snake and MSF are hired to investigate the threat, unveiling a rogue plot centered on the Peace Walker, an AI-powered nuclear-equipped weapon.

cards.heading: Mother Base and cooperative missions
cards.text: Initially supposed to be developed by other staff members, Kojima took the role of director simultaneously with Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots (2008) in order to target the game to a younger demographic of players. The game expands on series mechanics with traditional stealth action missions and a new "Mother Base" management system, where players recruit soldiers, research gear, and expand their military force. Peace Walker also has multiplayer functionality, featuring cooperative story missions and competitive team battles.

cards.heading: Reception and the HD Collection
cards.text: Peace Walker received critical acclaim for its narrative, base management and scale on PSP. It later appeared in the 2011 Metal Gear Solid HD Collection. Ground Zeroes continued Snake's story in 2014.

main.title: Lost Planet 2
main.summary: Capcom returns to E.D.N. III ten years after the first Lost Planet, with new environments, enormous Akrid and cooperative uses for Vital Suits.

cards.heading: Capcom returns to Lost Planet ten years after the first story
cards.text: Capcom released Lost Planet 2 for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in May 2010, followed by Windows in October. Set ten years after Lost Planet: Extreme Condition, it returns to E.D.N. III as a changing climate reshapes the planet. The game sold more than 1.5 million copies worldwide.

cards.heading: Vital Suits and versus customization expand combat
cards.text: Large Akrid battles and mechanised Vital Suits return. Some suits allow one player to pilot while others ride alongside and fire, making the machinery part of cooperative combat. Flying suits add another way to move through the terrain. Competitive multiplayer also expands its customisation, with separate choices for a character's face, torso and legs.

cards.heading: A changed climate reshapes the conflict over thermal energy
cards.text: One decade on from the events of the first game, the climate of E.D.N. III has undergone drastic changes that have produced radically different biomes across the planet. These new circumstances have not stalled the ongoing conflict between various human factions to gain control of the planet's supply of Thermal Energy (T-ENG), whilst the indigenous Akrid creatures have begun to metamorphosise into new, unexpected forms. The most dangerous of these are colossal Akrid, classified as "Category G", that contain immense amounts of T-ENG and can alter the landscape of the environment by virtue of simply existing.

main.title: Alan Wake
main.subtitle: Light against the Taken
main.summary: Remedy makes light essential to surviving Bright Falls: the flashlight strips protection from enemies, while illuminated places offer shelter.

cards.heading: Alan reaches Bright Falls
cards.text: Remedy's Alan Wake follows a writer facing a story that can alter reality. Flashlights, street lamps and generators provide practical ways to survive the forests around Bright Falls. Light removes the darkness protecting many enemies and marks places where Alan can recover.

cards.heading: Removing the Taken's protection
cards.text: The Taken resist ordinary weapons until their dark protection is burned away. Alan must aim the flashlight at an enemy before finishing the attack with a firearm. Batteries limit how long he can intensify the beam, making distance and target priority important while enemies approach.

cards.heading: Finding a light in the forest
cards.text: A distant lamp can guide Alan through a dangerous forest and promise a safe place to stop. Reaching a lit area offers recovery and can interrupt pursuit. Generators and illuminated buildings become landmarks, separating exposed journeys from moments of relief.

cards.heading: Keeping the darkness away
cards.text: Batteries, generators, dark barriers and pools of light carry the story's conflict into repeated actions. Alan's equipment gives him a way to push through the threatening landscape. The player learns to search for illumination as carefully as ammunition.
